children: The Indian rupee opened higher by 16 paise at 95.01 per dollar on September 1, compared with Monday’s close of 95.17.

According to Finrex, rupee to open at 95.10 and stay in the range of 95 to 95.50 for the day. The RBI positioning increased from oversold positions of $ 103 billion in June to $ 137 billion in July-2026. This will keep the market largely bid on the dollar with RBI positioning for 1-3 month at $ 7.32 billion and 3 months to 1 year at $ 24.75 billion which is about $ 3 billion per month.
Exporters need to wait to sell dollars while importers may buy these dips with oil prices above $ 91.25 per barrel and dollar index at 99.50 levels, it added.
Asian currencies were mixed against the US dollar, with the Indonesian Rupiah gaining 0.29% and the Japanese Yen rising 0.09%.

The South Korean Won slipped 0.04%, while the Philippines Peso declined 0.10%. The Thai Baht fell 0.19%, and the Taiwan Dollar weakened 0.17%. The China Renminbi eased 0.14%, while the Malaysian Ringgit dropped 0.20%. The Singapore Dollar also edged lower by 0.02%.

The dollar held steady near a two-week high on Monday as markets ramped up bets on a rate hike after hawkish remarks by Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh, while the yen slipped back through the closely watched 160-per-dollar level.

title: Currency Check: Rupee opens 16 paise higher at 95/dollar; Asian peers trade mostly lower
